**Key components of Alphabet’s “Google Services” segment** Alphabet describes the Google Services segment as the combination of two broad revenue streams: | Revenue stream | What it includes (as disclosed in the 10‑K) | |----------------|--------------------------------------------| | **Google advertising** | • Google Search & other (search, Gmail, Maps, Play, Android, Chrome, etc.)
• YouTube ads (advertising shown on YouTube properties)
• Google Network (ads on partner sites via AdMob, AdSense, Google Ad Manager) | | **Google subscriptions, platforms & devices** | • Consumer subscriptions – primarily YouTube services (YouTube TV, YouTube Music & Premium, NFL Sunday Ticket) and Google One
• Platforms – revenue from Google Play sales of apps and in‑app purchases
• Devices – sales of Pixel phones, Pixel Watch, Nest, etc. | These definitions appear in both the FY 2024 and FY 2025 Form 10‑K filings: * FY 2025 “Google Services includes products and services such as ads, Android, Chrome, devices, Google Maps, Google Play, Search, and YouTube” and “consumer subscriptions … YouTube services, Google One; platforms … Google Play; devices … Pixel”【source 0】. * FY 2024 “Google Services includes products and services such as ads, Android, Chrome, devices, Google Maps, Google Play, Search, and YouTube” and “consumer subscriptions … YouTube services, Google One; platforms … Google Play; devices … Pixel”【source 5】. **YouTube advertising revenue change FY 2024 → FY 2025** The 10‑K tables of revenue by type show the following YouTube‑ads figures (in millions of dollars): | Fiscal year | YouTube ads revenue | |-------------|---------------------| | FY 2024 | $36,147 M | | FY 2025 | $40,367 M | Thus, YouTube advertising revenue **increased by $4.2 billion** (≈ 11.6 % growth) from FY 2024 to FY 2025.
